title: Shifters by Benedict Lombe at the Cherry Lane Theatre #shiftersplay #...
transcript: Do not see this play unless you want to rethink your entire life. Shifters is the latest offering from the Cherry Lane Theatre in the West Village, an intimate two-hander that's kind of devastating in its restraint. Des and Dre met when they were 16 and now they're 32, reuniting at the funeral service for Dre's grandmother. The play switches between the present day and a chronological retelling of their shared history. While it initially appears to be about romantic love and second chances, it blossoms into a much broader story about free will, cosmic forces and the butterfly effect, reminiscent of the film Past Lives. The two actors, Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra, are absolutely magnetic together, and their humorous variations in the cadence of their line deliveries are a major highlight of their performances. The way the characters naturally communicate is playful and witty, and yet with so much ease comes level of honesty that sometimes slips out unintentionally. There are plenty of overtly poetic moments, but they feel a little forced and they're nowhere near as impactful as the blunt, vulnerable truths that come out when their emotional walls are left undefended. These moments seem to sneak up and surprise them as much as they surprise us, but they're the meat of the entire piece — the wondering, the overthinking, the questions we think we shouldn't ask. This play illuminates how arguably every decision we make increases the already infinite possible ways our lives will play out, and how loving isn't necessarily big romantic gestures or uncontrollable sparks — it just means truly seeing someone. Shifters is not a perfect play — parts of the structure and narrative devices aren't my favorite, but these performances won me over, along with the simple but elegant direction that universalizes the story and taps into its expansive thematic potential. With that, another program for my collection.
